claims.text: The untreated MoNbTaW-based refractory high-entropy alloy has high strength but limited ductility and nonuniform deformation.
Annealing at approximately 800°C for 30 minutes under an oxygen partial pressure of approximately 10^-5 atm is the proposed intervention.
The specified annealing treatment will introduce a calibrated concentration of interstitial oxygen into MoNbTaW.
Interstitial oxygen introduced under these conditions will form oxygen-stabilized planar defects or small interstitial clusters.
The oxygen-stabilized defects or clusters will modify local bonding characteristics.
The oxygen-stabilized defects will preserve the alloy's overall atomic ordering.
Interstitial oxygen will lower local energy barriers to dislocation motion by softening specific matrix sites.
Lower barriers to dislocation motion will cause earlier and more homogeneous activation of plastic deformation.
Homogeneous defect structures and dislocation accommodation can improve ductility and uniform elongation.
The treated alloy will retain its bulk BCC structure.
Relative to untreated MoNbTaW, oxygen treatment will increase uniform elongation and total ductility.
Oxygen treatment will produce a more uniform deformation profile under quasi-static loading.
Oxygen treatment will produce a more uniform deformation profile under dynamic loading.
The treated alloy will maintain yield and ultimate tensile strengths comparable to the untreated alloy.
The oxygen treatment will not reduce impact-induced energy release.
Tightly regulated temperature, exposure time, and oxygen partial pressure will avoid unwanted phase changes and embrittlement.
Oxygen levels significantly above the beneficial processing window may cause embrittlement or phase instability.
The beneficial oxygen-incorporation window in MoNbTaW has not yet been fully mapped.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing untreated controls with samples annealed across oxygen partial pressures near 10^-5 atm using tensile, impact, TEM, and XRD measurements.
Failure to improve ductility or uniformity, or any loss of strength or energy release, will falsify the hypothesis.
